newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Mosenergo looks at limiting voting rights.
newsitem.headline: Russia Mosenergo looks at limiting voting rights.

text.p: Russian power utility Mosenergo shareholders will vote on a board proposal to require investors acquiring more than one percent of shares to get board approval to use their voting rights, a spokesman said on Monday.
Shareholders will vote on the measure and a proposal to authorise the board of directors to issue up to 800 million new shares at the April 21 annual meeting, the company said.

"Shares in the amount of more than one percent of the total maximum of voting shares, purchased after registration of the new charter by an individual or a corporate body ... without preliminary written permission from the board, will not participate in voting," the Mosenergo spokesman quoted the amendment offered by the board of directors as saying.
National power grid Unified Energy System (UES) which owns 49 percent in Mosenergo has a similar provision in its charter.
Mosenergo said in a statement shareholders would also vote on a proposal authorising the board to issue up to 800 million new shares to be sold at market price.

"We want to have a chance to have a quick instrument in our investment programme financing provided by financial markets, including the stock market," chief executive Nestor Serebryannikov said in the statemennt.
At 1230 GMT Mosenergo traded at $1.330 after $1.350 at Friday's close.
